newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN chief calls elections in Liberia crucial.
newsitem.headline: UN chief calls elections in Liberia crucial.

text.p: U.N. chief Kofi Annan, warning that peace and democracy in West Africa are fragile, said on Thursday that "free, fair and credible elections" next month in Liberia were the next crucial step to restoring the rule of law.
Annan also called for reversing the "illegitimate, misguided grab for power" by coup leaders in Sierra Leone "peacefully, if at all possible".
Annan sent his message from U.N. headquarters in New York to a ministerial meeting in Geneva of the Special Conference to Support the Peace Process in Liberia.
Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi reported to the meeting on developments in the peace process and prospects for the July 19 poll there.
Diplomats noted the irony of Ikimi taking part in the talks on Liberia's elections on the fourth anniversary of an annulled presidential poll in his country.

Participants, who discussed stalled funding of the election, included member countries of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), donor countries and other U.N. bodies assisting the peace process. Foreign ministers of Liberia, Ivory Coast, Burkina Fasso and Zimbabwe were among those attending.
"We have all been reminded in these last few weeks of the fragility of peace and democracy in West Africa," Annan said, referring to a May 25 coup in Sierra Leone.

"I have just returned from the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit in Harare and I can report that Africa is speaking with one voice in support of democracy and against the rule of the gun," the Ghanaian added.
The one-day ministerial meeting, being chaired by Ibrahima Fall, assistant U.N. secretary-general for political affairs, was the third since last November.
"Your Conference signals the determination to restore lasting security and the rule of law to Liberia," Annan said. "Free, fair and credible elections are the next crucial step in this process.
"If we succeed -- as I am confident we will -- Liberia can become a model of post-conflict reconstruction involving national leaders, regional organisations and the United Nations.
"The hopes of the continent are with you," Annan said.
